style: soft 3D cartoon, top-down, warm and friendly

plainWhy.digit tiles (deep blue) and the point: IMAGES.md §2 digits and marks: each tile IS a written digit; an object behind a place-value digit (a chocolate square, a button) makes every digit look like one equal piece of a whole, the wrong model for place value (§2, skin that would teach a wrong model). The content colours (blue given, amber outline on the zero tile) also carry the meaning.
plainWhy.three rows of parts (Place value, Decima: IMAGES.md §2 marks: every part is a written number or fraction (6 ones, 0.8, 8/10) with plus signs; nothing the child shares, cuts, counts, pours or weighs, and the brief names no object.
plainWhy.tray of parts (300, 7, 9/10, 2/1000) and: IMAGES.md §2 marks: the dragged chips are written values of different widths, and the grey 0 is the lesson's mark; the brief's colour rule makes grey the zero's alone.
plainWhy.Split, Join, number pad, running count: IMAGES.md §2 chrome and digits: controls and numerals, no object.

themeWhy: No skin, so no theme: the runtime's standard DEFAULT_THEME (chocolate keys, berry Enter) applies.
